item.text:
**Verdict:** yes, strongly. In 2024 Putin translated the program into named targets, deadlines, budgets, appointments, and enforcement tools, but the implementation channel was a centralized power vertical rather than independent institutions.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Executive Order on Russia’s development goals through 2030 and for the future until 2036 | President of Russia | 2024-05-07 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73986 | Sets a formal national plan and tells the government to submit a unified plan, develop a spatial-development strategy, prepare an infrastructure plan through 2036, and ensure priority annual budget allocations. The Presidential Executive Office and State Council are assigned monitoring duties. | 8B.2; 8B.1 |
| Positive | List of instructions following Presidential Address to the Federal Assembly | President of Russia | 2024-03-30 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/assignments/orders/73759 | Converts the address into measurable targets with deadlines: top-four GDP by PPP by 2030, poverty below 7%, 2% of GDP for R&D, higher manufacturing value added, lower import dependence, more domestic high-tech output, and infrastructure repairs. | 8B.2; 8B.1 |
| Positive | Government will send additional financing to support medical workers in rural areas | Government of Russia | 2024-12-18 | https://government.ru/docs/53769/ | Extends `Zemsky Doctor` and `Zemsky Paramedic` through 2030, raises compensation, allows one intra-regional transfer, and says roughly 2,000 specialists were brought in during 2024. This is concrete staffing policy with funding and a time horizon. | 8B.2 |
| Positive | Annual family payment law for citizens with two or more children | Government of Russia | 2024-07-13 | https://government.ru/docs/all/154255/ | Creates a nationwide annual family benefit for households with at least two children. This is a specific distributional instrument, not just rhetoric about family policy. | 8B.2 |
| Positive | Putin taps civilian economist to run defence | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-05-13 | https://theprint.in/world/putin-taps-civilian-economist-to-run-defence/2081878/ | Replaces Shoigu with Andrei Belousov to improve defence spending efficiency and innovation. That shows program-to-personnel translation in a major portfolio, though still inside a loyalist system. | 8B.2; 7B.5 |
| Positive | Putin appoints Patrushev and Dyumin as Kremlin aides | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-05-14 | https://theprint.in/world/putin-appoints-patrushev-and-dyumin-as-kremlin-aides/2084276/ | Moves long-time security insiders closer to the centre and keeps the core Kremlin circle intact. This is a concrete institutional staffing move, but it reinforces loyalty control more than autonomous governance. | 8B.2; 7B.5 |
| Positive | Executive Order approving the Basic Principles of State Policy of the Russian Federation on Nuclear Deterrence | President of Russia | 2024-11-19 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/75598 | Formalizes nuclear-use conditions and the threat set to be deterred. That turns strategic aims into an explicit doctrine and command framework. | 8B.2; 8B.1 |
| Positive | Putin signed law requiring social-media owners to provide user information to Roskomnadzor or the FSB | President of Russia | 2024-08-08 | https://en.special.kremlin.ru/acts/news/74828 | Builds an enforcement mechanism for information control by requiring user data disclosure and registration of large accounts. This is concrete institutionalization of regime control, not just messaging. | 8B.2; 7B.7; 7B.10 |
| Mixed | Russian economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | The reported growth and record-low unemployment were driven heavily by military production, showing that the 2024 program was implemented through wartime industrial mobilization rather than broad civilian development. | 8B.2 |
| Negative | Putin lets economically significant entities limit information disclosures | Reuters | 2024-01-29 | https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-lets-economically-significant-entities-limit-information-disclosures-3315001 | Weakens transparency and outside scrutiny for major firms, reducing the openness needed for independent correction or evaluation of the program. | 8B.2; 7B.7; 7B.10 |
| Negative | Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Describes power concentrated in Putin’s hands, weak transparency, and day-to-day decisions made by a small closed circle. That suggests the program is enforced from above, not through accountable institutions. | 8B.2 |
| Mixed/Negative | Russia’s 2024 budget spending factbox | Reuters via Kelo / Reuters | 2024-03-11 | https://kelo.com/2024/03/11/factbox-putin-pledges-over-126-billion-in-public-spending-as-election-looms/ | Reuters reported more than 11.5 trillion roubles in promised six-year infrastructure/social spending, but also that military spending would exceed social spending in 2024. This shows real budget translation, but one skewed toward war priorities. | 8B.2 |

Search gap: I found strong evidence for translation into plans, budgets, appointments, and enforcement, but little sign of independent auditing, open performance review, or durable institutional checks. The monitoring bodies named in the executive order are themselves part of Putin’s vertical, so the main limitation is not absence of implementation but absence of independent constraint.
